help.title: Help and guide
help.a1: Scores are awarded automatically: the AI system analyses your uploaded file against the standard criteria (or the criteria your teacher set). Each criterion is graded separately, and the final score is their weighted sum.
help.a2_1: Make sure the file fully covers everything the assignment asks for.
help.a2_2: Make sure the text is highly original (no plagiarism).
help.a2_3: Clearly show the outcome of the work (program output, a screenshot, a test result).
help.a2_4: Clearly explain how and why the work was done this way.
help.lowers: Why the AI lowers a score:
help.l1: Plagiarism or text copied from the internet.
help.l2: Content that does not match what the assignment asked for.
help.l3: No logical connection between the result and the explanation.
help.raises: Why the AI raises a score:
help.r1: Deep analysis of the problem being studied.
help.g5: All tasks completed correctly and in full
help.g2: Many errors, sections filled in only formally
help.g1: The answer is incomplete or off-topic
help.tc1: The full content of the main file the student uploaded.
help.tc2: Images, screenshots and diagrams embedded in the file (if any).
help.tc3: How well the work matches what the assignment asked for.
help.p1: If the file's content is empty or insufficient, the score drops significantly.
help.p2: If most of the assignment's requirements are not met, a high grade (4 or 5) is not possible.
help.p3: The file (and any diagram or image attached) must match the topic of the assignment.
help.strict1: Strict rule: if most of the file's content is empty or off-topic → the grade is no higher than 2.
help.strict2: Strict rule: if no file was uploaded at all, or its format cannot be read → no score is given.
help.adminIntro: The platform brings everyone involved in the teaching process into a single ecosystem.
help.roleAdmin: Administrator: you manage the whole structure — creating users, groups, departments and news. You see the full statistics.
help.roleTeacher: Teacher: creates assignments, uploads literature and tracks how their groups are doing.
help.roleStudent: Student: receives assignments, submits solutions, and sees their grades and the literature available.
help.groupsHowCreateA: In the «Groups» section, click «Add group». Enter a name (for example, «IT-2024») and pick a curator from the list of teachers.
help.groupsHowAddA: Select a group from the list and click «Add student» in the right-hand panel. A student can only be in one academic group at a time — if they are in another group, they are moved automatically.
